test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 31 May 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: How many seats were reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha for the 2019 general election?
solution:
The correct answer is** __47__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the order issued by the** Delimitation Commission in 2008**, **412 are general, 84 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes, and 47 seats for the Scheduled Tribes.**
 
• For the 15th Lok Sabha elections, the number of seats reserved for scheduled tribes increased from **41 to 47.**
 
• Reservation in India is all about **reserving access to seats in government jobs, educational institutions, and even legislatures to certain sections of the population**.
 
• Also known as affirmative action, the reservation can also be seen as** positive discrimination**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 334** of the Constitution lays down the provisions of the Constitution **relating to the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.**
 
• All voters, **including Non-SC, and Non-ST community voters**, have the **right to vote for these candidates belonging to SC or ST candidates** if contesting from their constituency.** About 25% of the Indian population belongs to SC/ST communities.**
 
• **About the same ratio of seats are reserved for them in the Parliament.**
